contexts.japanese:

しかし、妾にとってはそれだけ意味がある取引だということだ」

「そなたにとってはまったく大したことではないかもしれない。

contexts.WH: "It probably isn't that big a thing for you at all.  However, that is the only meaningful transaction as far as I am concerned."
contexts.MG:
"It may have been a truly trivial matter from your perspective.
However, the deal was important enough to me to be deserving of this reward."
contexts.UP:
"To you, it may not be that great a thing at all.
But that is how significant this transaction is to me."
contexts.note: MG says the bargain is important enough to Beatrice to deserve the reward; UP says that is how significant it is. Neither retains the invented exclusivity.

findings.sourceReading: Though the transaction may seem trivial to Rosa, it has enough significance to Beatrice to justify her offer.
findings.alternative: だけ can mark exclusivity in other constructions, but here それだけ expresses extent/significance, contrasted with Rosa finding it insignificant.

findings.description: 痛みなくして癒しはない is rendered removing the pain is not healing, repeating the preceding distinction rather than its consequence.

contexts.japanese:
厳密には違う。
癒しとは痛みを取り除くことではない。
痛みに耐えた対価として支払われる快楽なのだ。
ゆえに、痛みなくして癒しはない。
癒しの悦びを知るには、痛みを知らなくてはならないのだ。
contexts.japanesePC: ゆえに、痛みなくして癒しはない。
contexts.japanesePS3:
厳密には違う。
癒しとは痛みを取り除くことではない。
痛みに耐えた対価として支払われる快楽なのだ。
ゆえに、痛みなくして癒しはない。
癒しの悦びを知るには、痛みを知らなくてはならないのだ。
contexts.WH: Therefore, removing the pain isn't healing.
contexts.MG:
Strictly speaking, that's not quite right.
Healing isn't the same thing as removing pain.
It's the pleasure we earn as compensation for withstanding pain.
Therefore, removing the pain isn't healing.
To know the joy of healing, you have to know the pain.
contexts.UP:
Strictly speaking, it's different.
Healing isn't the same thing as removing pain.
It's the pleasure earned for withstanding pain.
Therefore, there can be no healing without pain.
To know the joy of healing, you have to know the pain.
contexts.note: MG retains removing pain is not healing, which only repeats the prior distinction. UP correctly states that there can be no healing without pain.

findings.sourceReading: Since healing is pleasurable compensation for enduring pain, there is no healing without pain; one must know pain to know healing joy.
findings.alternative: The next sentence retains the prerequisite in knowing healing joy, but the first sentence itself substitutes a different proposition and obscures the inferential progression.

くっくっくっく…」

「となれば、……そなたの痛みに報いる悦びがいる。

contexts.WH: "In that case, ......there is joy as a reward for your pain.  You can boast of the suffering in your past.  Because you are qualified to know a kind of pleasure that those who have not known suffering cannot taste.  ...Those that have known this pleasure, cannot help but give the same joy to other people...  *cackle*cackle*..."
contexts.MG:
"Which means...you must know joy, in order to compensate you for your pain.
You should be proud of your past sufferings.

...Those who experience this pleasure...cannot help but pass on the same joy to others...

contexts.UP:
"In that case, ......you will require joy that compensates for your pain.
You can feel proud of the past you have suffered.

...Those that have known this pleasure cannot help but give the same joy to others...
*cackle*cackle*..."
contexts.note: MG changes the sentence but still says Rosa must know joy in order to compensate herself, rather than needing a pleasure that rewards her pain. UP correctly describes joy compensating for pain.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice concludes that Rosa needs joy to compensate for her pain, then describes qualification for pleasure and its transmission to others.
findings.alternative: The surrounding reward discussion implies availability, but いる here is need/require, not the existence of an already present reward.

findings.description: それをいつまでも引き摺る means continuing to dwell on, carry, or remain affected by those painful childhood memories. Dragged out forever suggests prolonging a process or story and does not idiomatically express their lingering hold.

contexts.japanese:

子どもの頃には少なからずの理不尽なこともあるものです。
そして、それをいつまでも引き摺っていてはいけない。
時と共に記憶の彼方に葬り、それを少しずつ忘れていくのが成長であり、大人になることだったはず。
だから大人になるということは、それら全ての記憶と決別することだったのです。

contexts.WH: A large amount of unreasonable things happened when I was a kid.
contexts.MG:
...Oh, but these were my memories from when I was a kid.
It's common for unfair things to happen between kids.
And you mustn't hold onto grudges for such things forever.
With time, those memories get buried away, and forgetting them bit by bit is supposed to be part of growing up and becoming an adult.
So becoming an adult is the same as separating yourself from all those memories.
contexts.UP:
......Oh, but these are my memories from when I was a kid.
Quite a lot of unfair things happen when you're a kid.
And you can't drag them out forever.
In time, you bury them away in the far reaches of memory, and forget them bit by bit; that is supposed to be what it means to grow up, and become an adult.
So becoming an adult is the same thing as separating yourself from all of those memories.
contexts.note: MG replaces dragging memories out with holding onto grudges, which restores lingering but narrows the burden to resentment. UP retains drag them out forever in an active construction.

When Mama stayed over with a man, Maria got lonely and unruly and made a mess of the room.  When Maria went to search by herself, she got lost, the police picked her up and Mama was shamed. contexts.MG:
"......After all, I'm always doing horrible things to you.
Even when you bring a man over, I can't stay quiet.
When you spend the night out with a man, I get lonely and unruly and make a mess of my room.
When I go to search by myself, I get lost, the police pick me up, and you're shamed.
When you don't come home for several days and I cry and have to be consoled by the neighbors, you're shamed."
"Because I'm like this, I'm a burden to Mama.
Sorry for being born.

Even when you brought a man over, I couldn't stay quiet.
When you stayed over with a man, I got lonely and unruly and made a mess of the room."
"When I went to search by myself, I got lost, the police had to pick me up and I brought shame on you, Mama.

"Because I'm like this, I cause trouble for you, Mama.
I'm sorry for being born.
So I'll become delicious oven‐baked apples for you, Mama."
contexts.note: Both editions retain making a mess of the room and soften Maria’s account of ruining it.

findings.sourceReading: Maria recalls becoming lonely and acting out when Rosa stayed away with a man, ruining the room.
findings.alternative: Make a mess of can range from untidying to severely damaging something, so the stronger reading remains possible.
